name: Stalled Deal Rescue Queue
value_proposition: Turn an open-deals export into a skip-ruled stall queue ranked by amount, with recovery notes that may use only export fields — the owner reviews and acts from their own CRM or email, and the kit never sends or writes back.
persona: Owner or sales lead at a 5-30 person agency, consultancy, or B2B service firm who keeps 10-40 open deals in HubSpot, Pipedrive, or a spreadsheet and only notices silent deals at month end.
problem: Open deals sit in a stage with no next step and no recent activity. The owner assumes no news is fine until the close date passes, then the amount disappears from the forecast.
workflow: 1. The person writes stall limits and skip rules before any queue: days-in-stage limit, days-since-activity limit, owner minimum amount, statuses that are never chased (default closed-won, closed-lost, on-hold), and deals to always skip. PERSON DECIDES: the limits, the minimum, and which statuses or deals never enter the chase list.

2. The person exports open deals as CSV with deal name, amount, stage, days in current stage, last activity date, next step, close date, and status, plus the export's as-of date. They open last week's outcome log. PERSON DECIDES: which columns to keep. Remove emails, phone numbers, and any columns the workflow does not need. This is an export review, not a live HubSpot, Pipedrive, Salesforce, or email connection.

3. The person checks the data settings of their AI assistant (chat history, training use, and file retention) before pasting or uploading anything. File upload support differs by ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini plan, account, and admin settings. PERSON DECIDES: whether to paste the rows as text, upload a file, or not use AI for this data at all.
4. The person pastes the Stall Queue Prompt and their rules from the Stall Limits and Skip Rules Worksheet, then attaches or pastes the export and the outcome log.

5. AI runs SKIP RULES FIRST. It sets aside closed-won, closed-lost, owner-marked on-hold, amounts below the owner's minimum, rows missing deal name or amount, and deals on the always-skip list. Every skipped row is listed with its reason. PERSON DECIDES: whether a below-minimum or on-hold deal should still be reviewed.

6. AI applies owner stall rules to remaining open rows: days in stage over the stage limit, or last activity older than the activity limit as of the export date, or next step blank. It ranks stalled deals by amount, largest first. Rows that are not stalled are listed as skipped with the reason 'not stalled under your rules'. PERSON DECIDES: whether a flagged row is actually stalled before any chase.

7. For each queued deal, AI cites only export fields as CONFIRMED and drafts one recovery note using only deal name, amount, stage, and last activity date. It does not invent a contact, objection, or deadline. It labels CONFIRMED, AI INTERPRETATION, and RECOMMENDED ACTION separately. PERSON DECIDES: whether each recommended action happens.

8. The person uses the Recovery Note Review Checklist and checks every CONFIRMED number against the export row. PERSON DECIDES: edit and send from their own email, update the next step in their own CRM, hold, or mark lost. The Blueprint never sends and never writes a CRM field. Outcomes (moved, still stalled, lost, on hold) go in the outcome log and feed next week's run.
before: The owner scrolls the pipeline when a report is due, pokes whichever deal they remember, and finds out a large one went quiet weeks ago.
after: Each week the owner reviews a stall queue with visible skip reasons, evidence cited from the export, and ready-to-edit recovery notes. Last week's on-hold and lost deals stay out of the chase list.

guided_demo.summary: A public, six-step walkthrough at /blueprints/ai-pipeline-risk-detector using a fictional four-row deal export dated as of 2026-05-11, with stall limits of 14 days in stage or 14 days since activity or blank next step, and a fictional owner minimum of $500. SKIP RULES FIRST skips Birchwood (below $500) and sets aside Pell & Co as not stalled. The ranked stall queue lists Northgate Clinic ($8,400) then Harbor Lane ($1,500), with CONFIRMED dates from the export and field-limited drafts. A fact-check shows Matches. Next week's outcome log keeps Harbor Lane skipped after it is marked on-hold. The demo ends on the owner sending. Confirmed facts, AI interpretation, and recommended actions are labelled with text, not color alone. Every deal, amount, and date is invented. No live HubSpot, Pipedrive, Salesforce, or email connection is attached.
steps: Step 1 of 6 - The export: show the fictional 4-row deal table (Northgate Clinic website rebuild, Pell & Co monthly books, Harbor Lane discovery, Birchwood retainers) with as_of 2026-05-11, owner_minimum 500, and stall_if days_in_stage > 14 OR last_activity more than 14 days before as_of OR next_step blank. Label the table invented. State that no live HubSpot, Pipedrive, Salesforce, CRM, or email account is attached.

Step 2 of 6 - Skip rules first: show the exact heading 'SKIP RULES FIRST'. List Birchwood retainers as SKIPPED with text containing '$400' and '$500'. List Pell & Co monthly books as SKIPPED with text containing '2026-05-09', 'next step', and 'not stalled'. Show that closed-won, closed-lost, and on-hold are also skip rules even when this export has no such row.

Step 3 of 6 - The ranked stall queue: show exactly 2 queued rows, Northgate Clinic website rebuild first then Harbor Lane discovery, ranked by amount largest first. Show CONFIRMED text containing 'Northgate Clinic', '8400' or '$8,400', 'proposal', '21', and '2026-04-18'. Show the draft 'Checking in on the $8,400 website rebuild proposal last touched April 18. Is this still useful to discuss?'. Show CONFIRMED text for Harbor Lane containing '1500' or '$1,500', 'qualified', '45', and '2026-03-20'. Show the draft 'The Harbor Lane discovery item for $1,500 has had no recorded activity since March 20. Should we close this out or set a next step?'. Show the text labels 'CONFIRMED', 'AI INTERPRETATION', and 'RECOMMENDED ACTION' as visible words, not as color or icon alone. Show AI INTERPRETATION text containing 'do not prove' and 'lost interest'. Show the exact sentence 'Do not invent a contact, objection, or deadline.'

Step 4 of 6 - Check the numbers: open the Northgate Clinic draft. A 'Check numbers against the export row' button shows three rows (amount $8,400 vs 8400, last activity 2026-04-18 vs 2026-04-18, days in stage 21 vs 21), each labelled with the text 'Matches'.

Step 5 of 6 - Next week's log: show the fictional outcome log for the week of 2026-05-11 with Harbor Lane discovery outcome on_hold and Northgate Clinic outcome still_stalled. Show a mock run as of 2026-05-18. Harbor Lane is SKIPPED with text containing 'on_hold' or 'on-hold'. Pell & Co and Birchwood stay skipped for the same reasons as step 2. Show the sentence 'Logged on-hold deals are not chased again.'

Step 6 of 6 - You send it: state the exact sentences 'You send it. Nothing is sent or written to the CRM.' and 'Do not invent a contact, objection, or deadline.' Explain that the person edits and sends from their own email or updates the next step in their own CRM, or decides not to, and that nothing is sent, edited, cancelled, or paid automatically. Offer a link to the Premium kit labelled as private preview with sign-in required.

guided_demo.fictional_data_notice: All deals, company names, amounts, stages, activity dates, and dates on this page are fictional. No real customer or pipeline data is used, and nothing is connected to HubSpot, Pipedrive, Salesforce, email, or any other live system.

kit_contents.title: Stall Queue Setup Checklist
kit_contents.purpose: Step-by-step setup for the weekly run. It covers writing stall limits and the owner minimum, exporting open deals as CSV with deal name, amount, stage, days in stage, last activity, next step, close date, status, and as-of date, removing emails and phone numbers, opening last week's outcome log, checking the AI tool's data settings before pasting or uploading, and the rule that this is an export review, not a live HubSpot, Pipedrive, or Salesforce connection. It notes that file upload support differs by ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini plan, account, and admin settings, and that rows can be pasted as text instead.

kit_contents.title: Stall Queue Prompt
kit_contents.purpose: Copyable prompt that runs SKIP RULES FIRST, lists every skip with its reason, applies owner stall rules, ranks remaining deals by amount largest first, drafts recovery notes using only deal name, amount, stage, and last activity date, and labels CONFIRMED, AI INTERPRETATION, and RECOMMENDED ACTION separately. It forbids inventing a contact, objection, or deadline, sending email, and writing CRM fields.

kit_contents.title: Week-to-Week Outcome Log Prompt
kit_contents.purpose: Copyable prompt for the following week. It reads the previous outcome log with the new export, skips rows whose log outcome is lost or on_hold, keeps still_stalled and moved rows labelled from the log, and forbids sending or writing CRM fields.

kit_contents.title: Stall Limits and Skip Rules Worksheet
kit_contents.purpose: Browser-only form where the person sets the days-in-stage limit, days-since-activity limit, owner minimum amount, statuses that are never chased, and deals to always skip. It generates a copyable rules block to paste with the prompts. Nothing is saved to Atlas.

kit_contents.title: Outcome Log Template
kit_contents.purpose: Column layout (week_of, deal, amount, action_taken, outcome, notes) with allowed outcome values moved, still_stalled, lost, on_hold, skipped_not_stalled, skipped_below_minimum, skipped_closed, and the fictional Harbor Lane on_hold and Northgate still_stalled rows from the guided demo. Includes a Copy CSV button so the person can start their own spreadsheet.

kit_contents.title: Recovery Note Review Checklist
kit_contents.purpose: Interactive, session-only checklist used before contacting anyone. It confirms that SKIP RULES FIRST ran, that every skip has a reason, that remaining rows are amount-ranked largest first, that CONFIRMED amounts and dates match the export row, that labels are separate, that the draft uses only deal name, amount, stage, and last activity, that no contact or objection was invented, that a stall flag was not treated as proof the deal is dead, and that the person will send or update the CRM themselves.

kit_contents.title: Fictional Sample Deal Export
kit_contents.purpose: The same fictional four-row deal CSV used in the guided demo, labelled as fictional, with a Copy CSV button. The person can practice the full workflow in their AI tool before using real pipeline data.

kit_contents.title: Data and Safety Guidance
kit_contents.purpose: Rules for handling CRM exports in AI tools: review data settings, remove emails and phone numbers, do not paste passwords or payment details, do not invent a contact or objection, do not treat a stall flag as proof the deal is dead, and do not chase deals logged as lost or on-hold. It also states that file upload support differs by plan and that nothing is sent or written to the CRM automatically.

decision_rules: Write SKIP RULES FIRST and apply it before stall scoring, ranking, or drafting any recovery note.
Skip any row whose status is closed-won, closed-lost, or on-hold (or any status on the owner's never-chase list). Show the reason 'status <status>'.
Skip any row whose amount is below the owner's minimum. Show the reason 'amount $<amount> is below your $<minimum> minimum'.
Skip any row missing deal name or amount. Show the reason 'missing deal name or amount' under NEEDS YOUR CHECK, not in the queue.
Skip any deal on the owner's always-skip list. Show the reason 'on your always-skip list'.

A remaining open deal is stalled when days_in_stage exceeds the owner's stage limit, or last_activity is older than the activity limit as of the export as_of date, or next_step is blank. Show which stall condition matched.
If a remaining open deal is not stalled under those rules, skip it with the reason 'not stalled under your rules'.
Rank stalled deals by amount, largest first. If two deals share an amount, older last_activity first.
Recovery notes may state only deal name, amount, stage, and last activity date from the export row. Do not invent a contact name, email, phone, objection, deadline, or competitor.
A stall flag is CONFIRMED missing activity or a missing next step in the export. It is not proof the buyer lost interest. That caution is AI INTERPRETATION.
Do not invent a 0-100 risk score. Use only the owner's written stall rules.
The draft is a draft only. Do not send it. Do not edit a CRM field. Suggest an outcome-log row; the person adds it.
On a later run, start from a new export and the current outcome log. Skip rows whose log outcome is lost or on_hold.
human_ai_boundary: AI applies skip rules and lists every skipped row with its reason. The person decides whether a below-minimum or on-hold deal should still be reviewed.
AI applies owner stall rules and ranks by amount. The person decides whether a flagged row is actually stalled before any chase.
AI drafts recovery notes using only export fields. The person checks every number against the export row, edits the wording, and approves it.
AI labels a stall as missing activity, not as proof the deal is dead. The person decides whether to chase, hold, or mark lost.
AI never sends email and never writes a CRM field. The person sends from their own email or updates the next step in their own CRM, or decides not to.
AI reads the outcome log. Only the person records outcomes, and the log reflects what the person entered, not what AI assumed.
The person decides whether any recommended action happens.
safety: Nothing is sent, edited, cancelled, or paid automatically. Every page states that the person sends it, and that nothing is sent or written to the CRM.
Atlas does not connect to HubSpot, Pipedrive, Salesforce, email, or any other vendor. It has no OAuth flow, no API call, and does not upload the person's data to any third party.

Before pasting or uploading exports to an AI tool, the person is told to review that tool's data settings (such as chat history, training use, and file retention) and to remove emails, phone numbers, and other columns the workflow does not need.
The kit tells the person not to paste account passwords, payment card numbers, or bank details into the AI tool.
File upload support and data controls in ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini differ by plan, account, and admin settings. The kit says so and does not claim any plan includes a specific capability.
The kit tells the person not to invent a contact, objection, or deadline, not to treat a stall flag as proof the deal is dead, and not to chase deals logged as lost or on-hold.
All demo and sample data is fictional and labelled as fictional on the page.
Worksheet entries and checklist progress stay in the browser session only and are not saved to Atlas.
The pages contain no statistics, win-rate claims, savings, ROI claims, prices, or checkout. The only dollar figures are the fictional deal amounts and the fictional $500 minimum.
required_data_tools: CRM or spreadsheet export of open deals (CSV) with deal name, amount, stage, days in stage, last activity date, next step, close date, and status
Owner-set stall limits (days in stage, days since activity) and owner minimum amount
Outcome log spreadsheet, started from the kit's Outcome Log Template
The owner's own email or CRM for any follow-up
A file-capable AI assistant. File upload support differs by plan, account, and admin settings; rows can be pasted as text instead.

constraints: Private preview only. The guided demo lives at /blueprints/ai-pipeline-risk-detector and the Premium kit at /blueprints/ai-pipeline-risk-detector/kit. Both pages set robots noindex and are not linked from the homepage, header navigation, or the sitemap.

The Premium kit requires requireUser from src/lib/auth.ts and hasActiveEntitlement for this product. It is labelled "Premium · Private preview". It shows no Stripe price, checkout, or Buy Premium unless the product is already in PAID_PRODUCTS.
All sample data is fictional and labelled as fictional. No live connector, OAuth flow, API call, or upload to a third party.
AI prepares; the person decides. Confirmed facts, AI interpretation, and recommended actions are labelled separately. Nothing is sent, edited, cancelled, or paid automatically.
No invented statistics, savings, or ROI claims. ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini capabilities differ by plan; say so where it matters.

Product files live in app/blueprints/ai-pipeline-risk-detector/, components/premium/ai-pipeline-risk-detector/, and src/lib/premium/ai-pipeline-risk-detector/. Register the Blueprint in src/lib/blueprints.ts. Do not edit Daily Inbox, Collections product behavior, Stripe, or Production.
e2e/ai-pipeline-risk-detector/authenticated.spec.ts is read-only once it exists. Do not skip, weaken, or rewrite it. Authenticated QA uses automatic session refresh.
Keyboard accessible, visible labels, no horizontal scrolling at a phone-sized viewport, no console errors.
